items.label: f03-schema-change
items.front: Safe schema change guidance for NetSlack (no Migrations folder yet).
items.back: 1) Use migrations instead of EnsureCreated; 2) backfill nullable columns before making them required; 3) add indexes concurrently where supported; 4) test query behavior before changing relationships; 5) plan rollback and data retention.

items.label: f01-error-contract
items.front: NetSlack error contract, from exception to client.
items.back: AppException subtypes (NotFound, Forbidden, Conflict) plus ArgumentException are mapped by ExceptionHandlingMiddleware to 404/403/409/400 with the message as Title and Detail; anything else is a logged 500 with a generic message; every body carries a traceId that http.ts parses into ApiError.

items.label: f04-auth-trace
items.back: JwtTokenService signs claims (dev auth only) -> AddJwtBearer validates the token -> CurrentUser turns claims into ICurrentUser -> ChannelService/MessageService do resource authorization (the core IDOR check).

items.label: f02-reactions-drill
items.front: Data-model drill: what must a plan for message reactions name?
items.back: Table, composite key, delete behavior, indexes, DTO changes and tests, anchored to MessageConfiguration.cs and MessageDto.cs.

items.prompt: The private UserProfile() constructor used by EF sets DisplayName, Email and AvatarUrl to string.Empty. What happens if those three lines are deleted?

choices.text: The build fails, since TreatWarningsAsErrors makes CS8618 an error
Nothing at build time; the compiler only checks public constructors
The build passes, but each profile then loads with null strings
EF throws at startup, since it needs every string property set to a value

choices: The build fails, since TreatWarningsAsErrors makes CS8618 an error
Nothing at build time; the compiler only checks public constructors
The build passes, but each profile then loads with null strings
EF throws at startup, since it needs every string property set to a value

items.explanation: Directory.Build.props enables Nullable and TreatWarningsAsErrors. A constructor that leaves a non-nullable string property unset raises CS8618, and with warnings as errors the build stops. The nullable analysis covers private constructors too; EF does not require the initial values (it sets properties when it materializes rows).

items.prompt: A user posts a message whose body is only spaces. What is the Title of the problem response?

choices.text: One or more validation errors occurred.
body is required. (Parameter 'body')
The body field is required.
Unexpected server error.

choices: One or more validation errors occurred.
body is required. (Parameter 'body')
The body field is required.
Unexpected server error.

items.explanation: Guard.AgainstEmpty throws new ArgumentException("body is required.", "body"). The middleware maps ArgumentException to 400 and uses exception.Message as the Title, and since .NET Core 3.0 ArgumentException.Message appends " (Parameter 'body')" when a paramName is given. The 500 title is used only for unmapped exceptions, and the ASP.NET validation title is never produced here.

items.prompt: A NetSlack JWT expired 90 seconds ago and is sent to a REST endpoint. What happens?

choices.text: It is rejected, because ClockSkew is set to one minute here
It is accepted, because ValidateLifetime is set to false here
It is rejected only if the signing key has changed since then
It is accepted, because JwtBearer allows five minutes of skew

choices: It is rejected, because ClockSkew is set to one minute here
It is accepted, because ValidateLifetime is set to false here
It is rejected only if the signing key has changed since then
It is accepted, because JwtBearer allows five minutes of skew

items.explanation: AddJwtBearer sets ValidateLifetime = true and ClockSkew = TimeSpan.FromMinutes(1), replacing the five-minute default. 90 seconds past exp is beyond that, so the token fails lifetime validation and the request gets 401. The key is irrelevant to an expired token.

items.prompt: A DbUpdateException escapes MessageService while saving. What does the client receive?

choices.text: A 500 whose detail carries the exception message, to aid in debugging
A 409, since every database failure is mapped to a conflict
A 400, because DbUpdateException derives from ArgumentException
A 500 with a generic title and detail; the real error is only logged

choices: A 500 whose detail carries the exception message, to aid in debugging
A 409, since every database failure is mapped to a conflict
A 400, because DbUpdateException derives from ArgumentException
A 500 with a generic title and detail; the real error is only logged

items.explanation: The switch has no arm for DbUpdateException, so it falls to 500. For 500 the middleware logs the exception and writes "Unexpected server error." / "The request failed unexpectedly." instead of the message; the trace table calls this intentionally generic. Only ConflictException maps to 409, and DbUpdateException is not an ArgumentException.

items.prompt: EnsureCanReadChannelAsync loads the channel with AsNoTracking, but EnsureCanPostChannelAsync does not. Why does posting need the tracked load?

choices.text: Join adds a member to the channel, which the later save must persist
AsNoTracking would make the channel query skip the unique index
Without tracking, Include(item => item.Members) returns no rows
A tracked load locks the channel row until SaveChanges completes

choices: Join adds a member to the channel, which the later save must persist
AsNoTracking would make the channel query skip the unique index
Without tracking, Include(item => item.Members) returns no rows
A tracked load locks the channel row until SaveChanges completes

items.explanation: For a public channel, posting calls channel.Join, which adds a ChannelMember to the loaded aggregate. Only a tracked entity has its new member detected by SaveChangesAsync. Include works the same with or without tracking, indexes are unaffected, and EF takes no row lock on a tracked read.

items.prompt: A REST call to /api/channels/{id}/messages sends the JWT only as ?access_token=... with no Authorization header. What happens?

choices.text: 200: OnMessageReceived copies any query-string token into the context
401: the query token is read only for paths under /hubs/messages
403: query tokens are accepted, but they carry no user roles
200: JwtBearer reads ?access_token on every request path by default

choices: 200: OnMessageReceived copies any query-string token into the context
401: the query token is read only for paths under /hubs/messages
403: query tokens are accepted, but they carry no user roles
200: JwtBearer reads ?access_token on every request path by default

items.explanation: OnMessageReceived assigns context.Token from the query only when the path StartsWithSegments("/hubs/messages"), because browsers cannot set headers on a WebSocket. JwtBearer itself never reads the query string, so the REST call is unauthenticated and RequireAuthorization answers 401.

items.prompt: A workspace member posts a message to a public channel they have never joined. What happens?

choices.text: A 404, because the channel is hidden from non-members
The post succeeds, and they are saved as a channel member too
The post succeeds, but the member list stays unchanged
A 403, since only members of a channel may post in it

choices: A 404, because the channel is hidden from non-members
The post succeeds, and they are saved as a channel member too
The post succeeds, but the member list stays unchanged
A 403, since only members of a channel may post in it

items.explanation: EnsureCanPostChannelAsync loads the channel WITH tracking and, for a public channel, calls channel.Join(currentUser.UserId). The new ChannelMember is picked up by change tracking, so the single SaveChangesAsync inserts it with the message. The 403 path applies only to non-public channels, and not-found is only for a missing channel id.

items.prompt: Two different workspaces each create a channel named general. What does the schema allow?

choices.text: Both, because channel names have no index or constraint of any kind
Only one, since channel names are unique across the whole database
Only one, unless one of the two channels is created as a private one
Both, since the unique index covers WorkspaceId and Name together

choices: Both, because channel names have no index or constraint of any kind
Only one, since channel names are unique across the whole database
Only one, unless one of the two channels is created as a private one
Both, since the unique index covers WorkspaceId and Name together

items.explanation: ChannelConfiguration line 19 declares HasIndex(c => new { c.WorkspaceId, c.Name }).IsUnique(): names are unique per workspace, so the same name in two workspaces is fine and a duplicate inside one workspace is rejected. Channel type plays no part in the index.

items.prompt: A workspace member who is not in a private channel requests that channel's messages. What do they get?

choices.text: 200 with an empty list, since no rows match their access
401, because their token carries no claim for that channel
404, so that the private channel's existence stays hidden
403, with the detail "You do not have access to this channel."

choices: 200 with an empty list, since no rows match their access
401, because their token carries no claim for that channel
404, so that the private channel's existence stays hidden
403, with the detail "You do not have access to this channel."

items.explanation: EnsureCanReadChannelAsync throws ForbiddenException when the channel is not public and the user is not among its members, and the middleware maps ForbiddenException to 403 with the message as Title and Detail. NotFoundException is thrown only for a missing channel; nothing filters rows to an empty list, and the token authenticated fine.

items.prompt: Someone deletes a UserProfile who has written messages. What does the EF mapping make happen?

choices.text: The delete fails: Restrict blocks removing an author who has messages
The author's messages are deleted together with the profile row
The profile is removed and the messages keep a dangling AuthorId
The messages stay, with AuthorId set to null by the database

choices: The delete fails: Restrict blocks removing an author who has messages
The author's messages are deleted together with the profile row
The profile is removed and the messages keep a dangling AuthorId
The messages stay, with AuthorId set to null by the database

items.explanation: MessageConfiguration maps the AuthorId foreign key with OnDelete(DeleteBehavior.Restrict), so deleting a referenced profile is refused (EF throws for tracked dependents; otherwise the FK constraint fails the save). Cascade is used for the channel relationship, not the author, AuthorId is a non-nullable Guid so set-null is impossible, and the FK prevents dangling ids.

items.prompt: How does a ChannelType value appear in JSON over minimal-API responses and SignalR messages?

choices.text: As a number on both, since that is the default
As a lowercase name such as "public" on both
As its name, such as "Public", on both paths
As a number over HTTP and as a name over SignalR

choices: As a number on both, since that is the default
As a lowercase name such as "public" on both
As its name, such as "Public", on both paths
As a number over HTTP and as a name over SignalR

items.explanation: Program.cs adds a JsonStringEnumConverter twice: to ConfigureHttpJsonOptions (minimal API serialization) and to the SignalR JSON protocol's PayloadSerializerOptions. Each path needs its own registration, and both have one, so the client always sees strings. System.Text.Json's default would be numbers.

items.prompt: A correctly signed, unexpired token carries no NameIdentifier or sub claim. What does GET on a channel's messages return?

choices.text: 200, with the messages read as the user whose id is Guid.Empty
401 from JwtBearer, since it refuses any token that has no sub claim
500, because Guid.Parse throws on the missing claim value
403, because CurrentUser reports an empty id as not authenticated

choices: 200, with the messages read as the user whose id is Guid.Empty
401 from JwtBearer, since it refuses any token that has no sub claim
500, because Guid.Parse throws on the missing claim value
403, because CurrentUser reports an empty id as not authenticated

items.explanation: JwtBearer validates signature, issuer, audience and lifetime, so RequireAuthorization passes. CurrentUser.UserId uses Guid.TryParse and falls back to Guid.Empty, and IsAuthenticated also requires UserId != Guid.Empty, so it is false. EnsureCanReadChannelAsync then throws ForbiddenException, mapped to 403. The trace table says "unauthenticated", but the status is 403, not 401.

items.prompt: A client calls GET /api/channels/{id}/messages?take=500 on a channel with 2,000 messages. What comes back?

choices.text: The newest 100 messages, listed from oldest to newest
The oldest 100 messages of the channel, in order
A 400 error, since take must be no more than 100
All 500 newest messages, since take goes to SQL as sent

choices: The newest 100 messages, listed from oldest to newest
The oldest 100 messages of the channel, in order
A 400 error, since take must be no more than 100
All 500 newest messages, since take goes to SQL as sent

items.explanation: GetRecentAsync clamps take with Math.Clamp(take, 1, 100), orders by PostedAt descending, takes that many, then re-orders ascending before ToListAsync. So it returns the latest 100 in chronological order. Nothing rejects a large take, and the descending sort picks the newest, not the oldest.
